format: Text with inline TeX in $...$ and display TeX in $$...$$. Glossary symbol and units fields are TeX without delimiters.

cards.front: Reflection coefficient at normal incidence?
cards.back: $$\Gamma=\frac{E^r_0}{E^i_0}=\frac{\eta_2-\eta_1}{\eta_2+\eta_1}$$

cards.front: Transmission coefficient at normal incidence?
cards.back: $$\tau=\frac{E^t_0}{E^i_0}=\frac{2\eta_2}{\eta_2+\eta_1}=1+\Gamma$$

cards.front: $\Gamma$ for nonmagnetic media in terms of refractive index?
cards.back: $$\Gamma=\frac{n_1-n_2}{n_1+n_2},\qquad n=\sqrt{\varepsilon_r}$$

cards.front: How does the normal-incidence problem map onto a transmission line?
cards.back: Medium 1 is a line with $Z_0=\eta_1$; medium 2 is its load $Z_L=\eta_2$. $\Gamma$, the standing-wave ratio and the positions of maxima and minima all follow the same formulas.

cards.front: Reflected and transmitted power fractions at normal incidence?
cards.back: $$R=|\Gamma|^2,\qquad T=|\tau|^2\frac{\eta_1}{\eta_2}=1-R$$For lossless media.

cards.front: Field in medium 1 in front of a perfect conductor?
cards.back: $$\tilde E_1=E^i_0\left(e^{-jk_1z}-e^{jk_1z}\right)=-2jE^i_0\sin k_1z$$A pure standing wave with nulls every $\lambda_1/2$, starting at the conductor.

cards.front: Standing-wave ratio in medium 1?
cards.back: $$S=\frac{|\tilde E_1|_{\max}}{|\tilde E_1|_{\min}}=\frac{1+|\Gamma|}{1-|\Gamma|}$$

cards.front: How does a quarter-wave antireflection coating work?
cards.back: A layer $\lambda/4$ thick with $\eta_2=\sqrt{\eta_1\eta_3}$ makes the two reflections cancel, exactly like a quarter-wave transformer on a line. For nonmagnetic media, $n_2=\sqrt{n_1n_3}$.

cards.front: Snell's law of reflection and refraction?
cards.back: $$\theta_r=\theta_i,\qquad n_1\sin\theta_i=n_2\sin\theta_t$$

cards.front: Critical angle?
cards.back: $$\theta_c=\sin^{-1}\frac{n_2}{n_1}$$Exists only going from a denser to a less dense medium ($n_1>n_2$). Beyond it, all power reflects.

cards.front: What happens beyond the critical angle?
cards.back: Total internal reflection: $|\Gamma|=1$ for both polarizations. A field still exists in medium 2, but it decays away from the boundary and carries no average power across it.

cards.front: Numerical aperture and acceptance angle of an optical fibre?
cards.back: $$\sin\theta_a=\frac{1}{n_0}\sqrt{n_f^2-n_c^2}$$$n_f$: core, $n_c$: cladding.

cards.front: Plane of incidence?
cards.back: The plane containing the normal to the boundary and the direction of the incident wave.

cards.front: Perpendicular (TE) and parallel (TM) polarization?
cards.back: Perpendicular, or TE: $\mathbf{E}$ is normal to the plane of incidence. Parallel, or TM: $\mathbf{E}$ lies in the plane of incidence. Any wave is a sum of the two.

cards.front: Reflection coefficient, perpendicular polarization?
cards.back: $$\Gamma_\perp=\frac{\eta_2\cos\theta_i-\eta_1\cos\theta_t}{\eta_2\cos\theta_i+\eta_1\cos\theta_t},\qquad\tau_\perp=1+\Gamma_\perp$$

cards.front: Reflection coefficient, parallel polarization?
cards.back: $$\Gamma_\parallel=\frac{\eta_2\cos\theta_t-\eta_1\cos\theta_i}{\eta_2\cos\theta_t+\eta_1\cos\theta_i}$$$$\tau_\parallel=(1+\Gamma_\parallel)\frac{\cos\theta_i}{\cos\theta_t}$$

cards.front: Brewster angle for nonmagnetic media?
cards.back: $$\theta_B=\tan^{-1}\frac{n_2}{n_1}=\tan^{-1}\sqrt{\frac{\varepsilon_2}{\varepsilon_1}}$$$\Gamma_\parallel=0$ there. Nonmagnetic media have no Brewster angle for perpendicular polarization.

cards.front: What is special about $\theta_B+\theta_t$?
cards.back: At the Brewster angle, $\theta_B+\theta_t=90^\circ$: the reflected and transmitted rays are perpendicular.

cards.front: Why is light reflected at the Brewster angle polarized?
cards.back: Only the perpendicular component reflects, since $\Gamma_\parallel=0$. That is why polarized sunglasses cut glare off water and roads.

cards.front: Reflectivity and transmissivity at oblique incidence?
cards.back: $$R=|\Gamma|^2,\qquad T=|\tau|^2\frac{\eta_1\cos\theta_t}{\eta_2\cos\theta_i},\qquad R+T=1$$The cosines account for the change in beam cross-section.
